newsitem.title: CHINA: Hainan Air says wants bigger domestic share offer.
newsitem.headline: Hainan Air says wants bigger domestic share offer.

text.p: Hainan Airlines Co Ltd, a Chinese airline linked to financier George Soros, said on Monday it wants to offer up to 150 million shares to domestic investors to fund its expanding operations.
The airline had planned a much smaller offer of 17 million A shares but that was now seen as insufficient to meet its funding plans.
"We are a capital-intensive industry," said a spokesman, speaking from the company's headquarters in Haikou, capital of the island province of Hainan. "We need more capital."
The spokesman said the airline had sought approval from China's stock market regulators for an offer of 100 to 150 million shares and was awaiting approval.
Hainan Airlines has already listed 71 million B shares for foreign investors on the Shanghai stock exchange.
American Aviation, an investment fund partially owned by Soros, now holds about 21 percent of the airline's registered share capital.
The spokesman did not give details of the airline's planned uses for the funds from an expanded offer but it has said in the past it was considering setting up a new air cargo company.
The spokesman also said the airline's profits during the first half of the year were ahead of target, and that a recent airfare increase by all domestic carriers was helping earnings.
He did not give details but the airline has forecast after-tax profits of 140 million yuan ($16.8 million) for the full year.
"This is the big tourist season and we are doing well," said the spokesman.

However, the airline said it would delay paying its dividend on 1996 earnings until the A shares were issued. The payment would be made to all shareholders together with its dividend based on 1997 earnings.
